ANSWER TO THE OPEN QUESTION. No duration of skin anaesthesia was measured, for mepivacaine or for either lidocaine solution. What the study itself used is recorded in the paper card and in the D025 reason, which is where the exception for a paper's own open question allows it; here, [dose figure omitted] of mepivacaine was injected intradermally through a 25-gauge needle over 2.5 seconds by a blinded investigator. Skin anaesthesia was then recorded as the area insensitive to pinprick at 30 seconds and at 1, 1 1/2, 2 1/2, 3 1/2 and 4 1/2 minutes, and measurement stopped there; the area was still rising at the last reading for all six solutions. The abstract's 'duration of skin anesthesia' is not a measurement this study made: the duration half of that sentence rests on three cited references and on an uncontrolled impression from the authors' own emergency department. Two of those three references were looked up and are in extra_studies: Buckley 1985 (PMID 3158255) is a rat infraorbital nerve-block study, and DiFazio 1986 (PMID 3717616) is an epidural study reporting onset, not duration. Volume: the methods state the volume injected per intradermal wheal explicitly (recorded in the paper card and in the D006 claim update's reason under the brief's exception; written as [dose figure omitted] everywhere else). Endpoint: complete recovery, not half recovery - pinprick analgesia tested every 10 minutes 'until full recovery occurred', duration timed 'from the time of injection to the last reported analgesia at the site'. DESIGN SETTLED: double-blind, within-subject/paired (all 20 volunteers received all three solutions as separate volar-forearm wheals raised with a tuberculin syringe), paired Student's t test, n=20, healthy young volunteers, University of Kansas, Human Subjects Committee approval and informed consent. COMPARISON AND RESULT: bupivacaine alone 139 +/- 78 min, the mixture 36 +/- 16 min, chloroprocaine alone 24 +/- 11 min (mean +/- 1 SD). Mixture vs bupivacaine alone p < 0.001; mixture vs chloroprocaine alone ALSO significant at p < 0.01 - so the amide's contribution was greatly reduced but not statistically abolished, which two Notion pages get wrong. INJECTION PAIN - the point the task flagged. Pain WAS recorded, and the paper did NOT rank the three agents on it: 'During these experiments, stinging was a common experience with all test solutions.' (p. 589). That is the only pain sentence in the paper; no pain scale, no statistics, no ordering. The working hypothesis in my assignment - that this paper is 'the one that is cited' for the etidocaine-worse finding - is WRONG. The cited paper is Howe & Williams 1994, J Dermatol Surg Oncol 20(7):459-64, PMID 8034840, named as such in every citing passage in the record (bupivacaine-wheals, the comparison page, the wheal-literature page and 'What is still unsettled'), and its ordering is verified independently in Europe PMC: 'Lidocaine hurt least and etidocaine hurt most.'
